column1: # Entries are read in input order, then stably sorted by key and collapsed so that
# the last entry of a repeated key wins.  The consumed count is the same as in
# strict mode and the re-encoding is the canonical encoding of the normalised
# value.  Everything that is not map/set ordering is rejected exactly as in
# strict mode.  The last section switches back to strict mode and shows that the
# strict decoder rejects the non-canonical inputs used above.
# Maps: the last entry of a repeated key wins, whatever the order of the input.
# BTreeMap and HashMap: {1: 7} then {1: 9} gives {1: 9} (checked against borsh-rs)
# duplicate key 2 with another key between the copies
# a canonical input is returned unchanged
# Maps with other key and value types.
# the whole value of the last entry replaces the earlier one
# Result keys: Ok sorts before Err although its tag is larger
# Sets: unsorted elements are sorted, repeated elements collapse.
# BTreeSet and HashSet: {5, 5, 5} gives {5} (checked against borsh-rs)
# Err before Ok in the input; Ok first in the output (borsh-rs: 0200000001050001)
# Normalisation applies at every depth, and inside every element.
# the inner sets are normalised first, then the equal outer elements collapse
# Not lenient: everything else is rejected as in strict mode.
# the schema checks are the same in lenient mode
# Strict mode afterwards: the same inputs are rejected.
